mn106:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Kuru Country, at a town of the Kurus called Kammāsadamma.[^1]
mn106:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn106:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, sensual desires are impermanent, hollow, false, false-natured,
mn106:2.2: made up of illusion, and fools’ talk.
mn106:2.3: Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:2.4: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come—
mn106:2.5: are alike Māra’s realm, Māra’s domain, Māra’s bait, Māra’s hunting-ground.
mn106:2.6: Evil unprofitable notions of covetousness and ill-will and ambition lead on here, in this sensual desire sphere,
mn106:2.7: and they obstruct the training of a noble disciple here.
mn106:3.1: ‘Now, bhikkhus, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:3.2: “Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:3.3: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come—
mn106:3.4: are alike Māra’s realm, Māra’s domain, Māra’s bait, Māra’s hunting-ground.
mn106:3.5: Evil unprofitable notions of covetousness and ill-will and ambition lead on here, in this sensual desire sphere,
mn106:3.6: and they obstruct the training of a noble disciple here.
mn106:3.7: Suppose I were to abide with mind abundant and exalted, by transcending the world and resolving firmly with the mind:[^2]
mn106:3.8: then there would be no more evil unprofitable notions of covetousness and ill-will and ambition in me,
mn106:3.9: and with the abandoning of them my mind would be limited no longer; it would become measureless and well developed.”
mn106:3.10: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:3.11: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the Imperturbable,[^3] or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:3.12: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to one of the Imperturbable states.
mn106:3.13: This, bhikkhus, is called the first way directed to the Imperturbable.
mn106:4.1: ‘Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:4.2: “Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:4.3: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come;
mn106:4.4: whatever is form, all form is the four great primary elements and the form derived from the four great primary elements.”[^4]
mn106:4.5: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:4.6: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the Imperturbable, or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:4.7: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to one of the Imperturbable states.
mn106:4.8: This, bhikkhus, is called the second way directed to the Imperturbable.
mn106:5.1: ‘Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:5.2: “Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:5.3: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come;
mn106:5.4: forms here and now and forms in lives to come,
mn106:5.5: perceptions of forms here and now and perceptions of forms in lives to come—
mn106:5.7: What is impermanent is not worth relishing, not worth affirming, not worth accepting.”
mn106:5.8: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:5.9: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the Imperturbable, or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:5.10: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to one of the Imperturbable states.
mn106:5.11: This, bhikkhus, is called the third way directed to the Imperturbable.
mn106:6.1: ‘Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:6.2: “Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:6.3: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come;
mn106:6.4: forms here and now and forms in lives to come,
mn106:6.5: perceptions of forms here and now and perceptions of forms in lives to come;
mn106:6.8: Where these perceptions cease without remainder, that is more peaceful, that is a superior goal,
mn106:6.9: that is to say, the base consisting of nothingness.”
mn106:6.10: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:6.11: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the base consisting of nothingness, or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:6.12: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to the base consisting of nothingness.
mn106:6.13: This, bhikkhus, is called the first way directed to the base consisting of nothingness.
mn106:7.1: ‘Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple, gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, considers thus:
mn106:7.2: “This is void of self or of a self’s property.”[^5]
mn106:7.3: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:7.4: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the base consisting of nothingness, or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:7.5: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to the base consisting of nothingness.
mn106:7.6: This, bhikkhus, is called the second way directed to the base consisting of nothingness.
mn106:8.1: ‘Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:8.2: “I am not anywhere anyone’s owning; nor is there anywhere my owning in anyone.”[^6]
mn106:8.3: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:8.4: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the base consisting of nothingness, or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:8.5: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to the base consisting of nothingness.
mn106:8.6: This, bhikkhus, is called the third way directed to the base consisting of nothingness.
mn106:9.1: ‘Again, bhikkhus, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:9.2: “Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:9.3: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come;
mn106:9.4: forms here and now and forms in lives to come,
mn106:9.5: perceptions of forms here and now and perceptions of forms in lives to come;
mn106:9.6: perceptions of the Imperturbable, and perceptions of the base consisting of nothingness—
mn106:9.8: Where these perceptions cease without remainder, that is more peaceful, that is a superior goal,
mn106:9.9: that is to say, the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”
mn106:9.10: When he enters upon this way and abides in it often, his mind acquires confidence in this base.
mn106:9.11: Once there is full confidence, then he either enters upon the way to rebirth in the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, or else he decides to perfect understanding by reaching Arahantship.
mn106:9.12: On the dissolution of the body, after death, it is possible that that consciousness of his which leads on to rebirth may pass on, upon rebirth, to the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
mn106:9.13: This, bhikkhus, is called the way directed to the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.’
mn106:10.1: When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One:
mn106:10.2: ‘Venerable sir, here a bhikkhu enters upon this way:
mn106:10.3: “If I were not, and naught were mine, I shall not be and naught will be mine. And what there is, has come to be, that I abandon”,[^7]
mn106:10.5: Venerable sir, does such a bhikkhu attain final Nibbāna, or does he not?’
mn106:10.6: ‘Ānanda, one such bhikkhu might attain final Nibbāna, another such bhikkhu might not attain final Nibbāna.’
mn106:10.7: ‘Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why one might attain final Nibbāna and another might not?’
mn106:10.8: ‘Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu enters upon this way:
mn106:10.9: “If I were not, and naught were mine, I shall not be and naught will be mine. And what there is, has come to be, that I abandon”,
mn106:10.11: He relishes that equanimity, welcomes it, and holds to it.
mn106:10.12: As he relishes that equanimity, welcomes it, and holds to it, his consciousness comes to depend on it and to cling to it.
mn106:10.13: A bhikkhu who is affected by clinging, Ānanda, does not attain final Nibbāna.’
mn106:11.1: ‘But, venerable sir, when that bhikkhu clings, what does he cling to?’
mn106:11.2: ‘To the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, Ānanda.’
mn106:11.3: ‘It seems, venerable sir, that when that bhikkhu clings, he clings to the best of the objects for clinging?’[^8]
mn106:11.4: ‘When that bhikkhu clings, Ānanda, he does cling to the best of the objects for clinging.
mn106:11.5: For this is the best of the objects for clinging, namely,
mn106:12.1: ‘Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu enters upon this way:
mn106:12.2: “If I were not, and naught were mine, I shall not be and naught will be mine. And what there is, has come to be, that I abandon”,
mn106:12.4: He does not relish that equanimity, does not welcome it, and does not hold to it.
mn106:12.5: As he does not relish that equanimity, does not welcome it, and does not hold to it, his consciousness does not come to depend on it and does not cling to it.
mn106:12.6: A bhikkhu who is without clinging, Ānanda, attains final Nibbāna.’
mn106:13.1: ‘It is wonderful, venerable sir, it is marvellous!
mn106:13.2: For each stage, it seems, the crossing of the flood has been told to us by the Blessed One, depending on this, then on that.
mn106:13.3: But, venerable sir, what is the Noble One’s liberation?’
mn106:13.4: ‘Here, Ānanda, a noble disciple considers thus:
mn106:13.5: “Sensual desires here and now and sensual desires in lives to come,
mn106:13.6: perceptions of sensual desires here and now and perceptions of sensual desires in lives to come;
mn106:13.7: forms here and now and forms in lives to come,
mn106:13.8: perceptions of forms here and now and perceptions of forms in lives to come;
mn106:13.9: perceptions of the Imperturbable, perceptions of the base consisting of nothingness, and perceptions of the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—
mn106:13.10: that is embodiment, that is as far as embodiment extends.
mn106:13.11: This is the deathless, that is to say, the liberation of the mind through not clinging.’
mn106:14.1: ‘So, Ānanda, I have shown the way directed to the Imperturbable, I have shown the way directed to the base consisting of nothingness, I have shown the way directed to the base consisting of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, I have shown for each stage the crossing of the flood, depending on this, then on that, and I have shown the Noble One’s liberation.
mn106:15.1: ‘Ānanda, what should be done for his disciples out of compassion by a teacher who seeks their welfare and has compassion for them, that I have done for you, Ānanda.
mn106:15.2: There are these roots of trees, there are these empty huts. Meditate,[^9] Ānanda, do not delay, lest you regret it later. This is our instruction to you.’
mn106:15.3: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn106:15.4: The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
